baslik: The 'Absolutely Fireproof' Theatre That Became a Trap
tetik: a stage light igniting a curtain
mekanizma: a jammed fire curtain, blocked or confusing exits and doors that opened inward
ders: exit doors had to open outward and carry panic bars
yanilgi: The building was advertised as absolutely fireproof. The structure survived; hundreds of people didn't.
tartisma: The theatre opened before its safety equipment was finished. Who signs off on an opening?
basliklar: Why the Iroquois Theatre Fire Was So Deadly
The Fireproof Theatre That Trapped Its Audience
soru: Who signs off on an opening?
sahneler: Fire broke out on stage during a packed afternoon show in Chicago.
Within minutes, hundreds of people were dead, many of them children.
The theatre was advertised as absolutely fireproof.
A stage light set a curtain on fire.
The safety curtain jammed partway down.
Some exits were locked or hidden, and doors opened inward.
The crowd was trapped against them.
Exit doors afterward had to open outward with panic bars.

baslik: Pyrotechnics Ignited Soundproofing Foam in Seconds
sonuc: was engulfed by fire during a concert
tetik: stage pyrotechnics igniting foam on the walls
mekanizma: flexible polyurethane foam used as soundproofing burning extremely fast
ders: sprinklers became required in many existing nightclubs
yanilgi: The club wasn't large. The foam burned so fast that there were only minutes to get out.
tartisma: The foam was installed to quiet noise complaints. Who checks what goes on the walls?
basliklar: Why the Station Nightclub Fire Spread So Fast
The Foam That Turned a Concert Deadly
sahneler: During a concert, fire swept through a Rhode Island nightclub.
In minutes, one hundred people were killed.
The band's pyrotechnics sprayed sparks toward the walls.
The walls were covered in soundproofing foam.
That foam caught fire almost instantly.
Thick smoke filled the club.
The crowd rushed for the front door and was trapped.
Many existing nightclubs were then required to install sprinklers.

baslik: The Hotel Fire Where Smoke Killed People Floors Away
sonuc: burned, sending smoke through the tower
tetik: an electrical fault in a restaurant
mekanizma: fire in unsprinklered areas, with smoke spread through shafts, stairwells and ventilation
ders: Nevada required sprinklers in hotels and casinos
yanilgi: Most victims were nowhere near the flames. They died from smoke on upper floors.
tartisma: Sprinklers were left out of some areas to save money. How much is a sprinkler worth?
basliklar: Why the MGM Grand Fire Was So Deadly
The Smoke That Climbed a Hotel Tower
soru: How much is a sprinkler worth?
sahneler: Fire broke out in a Las Vegas hotel and casino.
Smoke spread through the tower, and eighty five people died.
It began with an electrical fault in a restaurant.
That area had no sprinklers.
Smoke rose through shafts and stairwells.
Most victims were floors above the flames.
They were overcome by smoke, not fire.
Nevada then required sprinklers in hotels and casinos.

baslik: The Munitions Pier That Exploded During Loading
sonuc: exploded while ships were being loaded with munitions
mekanizma: detonation of explosives during hurried, poorly supervised loading
ders: the Navy changed munitions-handling training and procedures
yanilgi: The workers had not been trained in handling explosives. Speed was prioritized.
tartisma: Sailors who refused to return to unsafe work were court-martialled. When is refusing unsafe work justified?
basliklar: Why the Port Chicago Pier Exploded
The Munitions Loaded Too Fast
sahneler: A munitions pier in California exploded as ships were being loaded.
The blast destroyed both ships and the pier, killing three hundred twenty men.
Loading was racing to meet targets.
Most sailors had no training in handling explosives.
Munitions detonated during the work.
Survivors who then refused unsafe work were court-martialled.
The case became a landmark in civil rights history.
The Navy changed its munitions-handling procedures.

baslik: A Rich Men's Club Weakened the Dam Above a Town
sonuc: burst and sent a flood into Johnstown
tetik: heavy rain overtopping a dam that had been modified
mekanizma: overtopping of an earthen dam whose crest was lowered and spillway obstructed
ders: the flood helped shift US law toward liability for dam owners
yanilgi: The rain didn't have to be catastrophic. The dam's owners had reduced its ability to pass floodwater.
tartisma: The club members were never held legally responsible. Should they have been?
basliklar: Why the South Fork Dam Failed
The Dam a Club Made Weaker
sahneler: A dam burst above Johnstown, Pennsylvania.
A wall of water destroyed the town, and two thousand two hundred nine people died.
The dam belonged to a private fishing club.
The club had lowered its crest to fit a road on top.
Fish screens partly blocked the spillway.
After days of rain, water poured over the top.
The earthen dam washed away.
The flood helped change US law on dam owners' liability.

baslik: The Spillway That Broke at America's Tallest Dam
sonuc: forced the evacuation of nearly 190,000 people
tetik: a hole opening in the main spillway chute
mekanizma: uplift and erosion under a thin, poorly drained concrete spillway slab
ders: California rebuilt the spillways and reviewed dam safety practices
yanilgi: The dam itself was never failing. Its spillways were, and that could have released the reservoir uncontrollably.
tartisma: Earlier reviews didn't challenge the original design. How often should designs be re-examined from scratch?
basliklar: Why the Oroville Dam Spillway Failed
The Crack That Evacuated a County
sahneler: At America's tallest dam, the main spillway broke apart.
Within days, nearly one hundred ninety thousand people were ordered to evacuate.
A hole had opened in the concrete chute.
Water was getting underneath the thin slab.
The emergency spillway was used for the first time.
Its hillside began eroding toward the top.
The dam itself held.
California rebuilt both spillways and reviewed its dam safety practices.

baslik: A Dam Known to Be Unsafe Failed in a Flood
sonuc: failed and flooded Michigan towns downstream
mekanizma: embankment failure by static liquefaction of the dam's sandy fill
ders: Michigan strengthened its dam safety programme
yanilgi: The dam had already lost its federal licence over spillway capacity concerns years before.
tartisma: Regulators knew the risks but ownership disputes delayed repairs. Who fixes a dam nobody wants to pay for?
basliklar: Why the Edenville Dam Failed
The Dam That Lost Its Licence Years Before
hook: It was known to be unsafe
soru: Who pays for an old dam?
sahneler: After heavy rain, the Edenville Dam in Michigan collapsed.
Within hours, floodwater forced thousands of people to evacuate.
The flood then overtopped the next dam as well.
Edenville had lost its federal licence years before.
Regulators worried its spillways couldn't pass a major flood.
Repairs were delayed by disputes over ownership and cost.
The embankment's sandy fill gave way.
Michigan then strengthened its dam safety programme.

baslik: The Italian Dam That Failed Weeks After Filling
sonuc: collapsed weeks after its reservoir was filled
tetik: poor-quality construction and a mid-build design change
mekanizma: failure of a multiple-arch dam built with substandard materials on a base designed for a different dam type
ders: Italy introduced stricter state control of dam design and construction
yanilgi: The dam wasn't old. It failed within weeks of its reservoir filling for the first time.
tartisma: Construction started before the design was approved. What should come first?
basliklar: Why the Gleno Dam Collapsed
The Dam Redesigned Halfway Through
sahneler: A new dam in the Italian Alps collapsed weeks after its reservoir filled.
A flood swept down the valley, killing hundreds.
The dam's design had been changed during construction.
Arches were built on a base meant for a different kind of dam.
Materials used were of poor quality.
When full, the arches gave way.
The engineers were later convicted.
Italy introduced stricter state control of dam building.

baslik: The Texas Grid Was Minutes From Total Collapse
sonuc: came within minutes of a total collapse
tetik: a winter storm freezing power plants and gas supplies
mekanizma: generation outages from unwinterized equipment and gas supply freeze-offs, forcing rolling blackouts
ders: Texas required generators and gas facilities to prepare for extreme cold
yanilgi: It wasn't one type of power plant. Gas, coal, nuclear and wind all had cold-related outages.
tartisma: Texas runs a largely isolated grid. Is independence worth less help in an emergency?
basliklar: Why the Texas Grid Nearly Collapsed
The Winter Storm That Froze the Power Supply
soru: Is an isolated grid worth it?
sahneler: During a winter storm, the Texas power grid nearly collapsed.
Suddenly, millions of homes lost power for days in freezing cold.
Operators were minutes from an uncontrolled blackout.
Many power plants were not built for extreme cold.
Gas wells and pipelines froze, cutting fuel to generators.
Every type of plant had cold-related outages.
Controlled blackouts kept the grid from total failure.
Texas then required power and gas facilities to prepare for cold.

baslik: The Floodwalls That Failed Before the Water Reached the Top
sonuc: failed and flooded most of the city
tetik: storm surge from Hurricane Katrina loading the canal floodwalls
mekanizma: floodwall failures from soil and design weaknesses at water levels below their design height
ders: the flood defences were rebuilt as a new risk reduction system
yanilgi: Many walls didn't fail because water went over them. They failed below their design height.
tartisma: The system was built piecemeal over decades. Can a patchwork ever be a single safety system?
basliklar: Why New Orleans' Levees Failed
The Floodwalls That Broke Too Early
sahneler: As Hurricane Katrina passed, the floodwalls of New Orleans broke.
Within hours, most of the city was underwater.
Many walls failed before water reached their tops.
Surge pushed on the canal floodwalls.
A gap opened behind the walls, letting water in underneath.
The weak soil below gave way.
The defences had been built piecemeal over decades.
They were rebuilt afterward as a new flood protection system.

baslik: A Bad Weld From 1956 Exploded Under a Neighbourhood
tetik: a pressure rise on a pipe with a defective weld
mekanizma: rupture of a pipeline section with a defective seam weld installed in 1956
ders: US pipeline operators had to verify records and pressure-test old lines
yanilgi: The pipe wasn't just old. Records described it as seamless when it actually had a defective weld.
tartisma: The company's records didn't match the pipe in the ground. How reliable are old records?
basliklar: Why the San Bruno Pipeline Exploded
The Weld Nobody Knew Was There
sahneler: A gas pipeline exploded under a California neighbourhood.
Fire destroyed dozens of homes, and eight people were killed.
The pipe section had been installed in 1956.
Company records said it was seamless.
In reality, it had a badly made weld.
When pressure rose, the weld tore open.
Escaping gas ignited in a huge fireball.
Operators then had to verify records and pressure-test old lines.

baslik: Sensors on an Abandoned Pipe Overpressured a Whole Gas Network
sonuc: had fires and explosions in dozens of homes
tetik: regulator sensing lines left on a pipe taken out of service
mekanizma: regulators opening fully after sensing low pressure on an abandoned main, overpressuring low-pressure lines
ders: gas work plans now need engineering review of sensing lines
zincir: OLD MAIN TAKEN OUT OF SERVICE
yanilgi: Nothing was leaking at first. The regulators were doing exactly what their sensors told them.
tartisma: The work plan didn't include the sensing lines. How detailed must a plan be?
basliklar: Why the Merrimack Valley Gas Explosions Happened
The Sensor Lines Left on a Dead Pipe
hook: The sensors read a dead pipe
soru: How detailed must a plan be?
sahneler: In Massachusetts, gas fires and explosions hit dozens of homes at once.
Within hours, houses burned across three towns, and one person was killed.
Workers had taken an old gas main out of service.
But sensing lines for the pressure regulators were still attached to it.
The regulators read zero pressure.
So they opened fully and flooded the network with high pressure gas.
Appliances and pipes couldn't handle it.
Gas work plans now need engineering review of these lines.

baslik: A Pipeline Inside a Drain Blew Open City Streets
sonuc: ripped open streets in a series of explosions
tetik: propylene leaking from a corroded pipeline in a drainage culvert
mekanizma: corrosion of a pipeline encased in a drainage culvert, leaking propylene into the sewer network
ders: Taiwan moved to map and relocate hazardous underground pipelines
yanilgi: The explosions weren't one blast. Gas travelled through the drains and ignited along kilometres of road.
tartisma: No single agency had a full map of the pipelines. Who maps what lies under a city?
basliklar: Why Kaohsiung's Streets Exploded
The Pipeline Hidden Inside a Drain
sahneler: At midnight, explosions tore open kilometres of streets in Kaohsiung.
Roads collapsed into trenches, and thirty two people were killed.
Residents had smelled gas for hours.
A pipeline carrying propylene ran through a drainage culvert.
Hidden there, it had corroded and begun to leak.
Gas filled the drains beneath the roads.
When it ignited, the streets blew apart.
Taiwan then worked to map and relocate hazardous pipelines.

baslik: Skipping Corrosion Control Put Lead in a City's Water
tetik: a new water source used without corrosion control
mekanizma: corrosive water stripping protective scale from old pipes and leaching lead
ders: lead service lines in Flint were replaced and federal lead rules were revised
yanilgi: The river water itself wasn't the main problem. Without a corrosion inhibitor, it attacked old lead pipes.
tartisma: Residents complained for months before officials acted. Who listens when citizens report a problem?
basliklar: What Caused the Flint Water Crisis
The Corrosion Control That Was Skipped
sahneler: The city of Flint, Michigan, switched its drinking water source.
Within months, lead was pouring from residents' taps.
The new water was more corrosive.
Normally, a corrosion inhibitor protects old pipes.
In Flint, it wasn't added.
The water stripped the protective layer inside lead pipes.
Residents complained for months before action was taken.
Lead pipes were replaced, and national lead rules were revised.

baslik: The Fire Firefighters Fought Without Horses
tetik: a warehouse fire in a dense district of tall buildings
mekanizma: fire spread through wooden mansard roofs, with low water pressure and a horse flu outbreak slowing engines
ders: Boston improved its water supply and building codes
yanilgi: Firefighters weren't slow by choice. An outbreak of horse flu meant engines had to be pulled by men.
tartisma: Rooftop styles spread the fire from building to building. Should fashion be regulated for safety?
basliklar: Why the Great Boston Fire Spread So Far
The Fire Fought Without Horses
sahneler: A warehouse fire spread through downtown Boston.
Within hours, the flames destroyed the commercial district.
Many buildings had tall wooden mansard roofs.
Fire jumped easily from roof to roof.
An outbreak of horse flu had sickened the city's horses.
Fire engines had to be pulled by men.
Hydrants also had low water pressure.
Boston then improved its water supply and building codes.
